title: Protocol schemas and contract test kit

patches.reason: Dijkstra used id(node) — a CPython memory address — to break equal-cost ties in the priority queue. Equal-cost routes are common on a street grid, so route choice varied per process and per episode, breaking replay determinism (PLAN.md M0) and cross-process EpisodeSpec equality (PLAN.md M4). Replaced with a stable key: the node's waypoint id when present, otherwise its rounded position. Path *costs* are unchanged; only which of several equally short routes is returned becomes deterministic.

findings.title: The nav preset silently overrides the requested step budget
findings.detail: DeliveryBenchEnvConfig sets dynamic_max_steps_mult=2.5 for the `nav` preset, so deliverybench_env.py:462 recomputes max_steps per seed from a chained BFS oracle and clamps it to at least 20. The max_steps a caller passes is a floor, not the enforced budget.
findings.impact: A benchmark instance that pins budgets.steps would not get the budget it pins, and truncation would be attributed to the wrong cause. PLAN.md 12.2 makes step budget a scoring budget, so this must be reconciled before M7 freezes instances.
findings.resolution: The adapter exposes effective_step_budget() and derives truncation from it rather than from the requested value. M4 must decide whether benchmark instances pin the static budget or record the dynamic one.

findings.title: Handler-level action failures are reported under `action_error`
findings.detail: The vendored env surfaces failed PICKUP/DROP_OFF/MOVE handlers as info['action_error'] (deliverybench_env.py:1001) and keeps the message in info['raw_info']['error']; there is no top-level 'error' key. An adapter reading info['error'] reports every handler failure as an accepted action.
findings.impact: Would have made ActionResult.status wrong for every failed task action, breaking PLAN.md M6's typed-feedback requirement and the invalid-action metric.
findings.resolution: found by the invalid-action test and fixed in _action_error(); covered by tests/test_runtime_adapter.py

findings.title: The vendored engine emits no event stream
findings.detail: PLAN.md 7 requires structured events and PLAN.md 13 builds the portal on an event protocol, but the vendored env returns only an info dict. The adapter synthesizes a minimal stream (step_completed, action_error) with ids derived from the episode and a monotonic counter.
findings.impact: Event granularity is currently far below what PLAN.md 13.1's timeline needs (no pickup, dropoff, hazard, or transport events). Richer events must come from the task layer at M4, not from more adapter inference.
findings.resolution: open; recorded so the portal work does not assume a richer stream exists

findings.title: Reward arrives as one scalar with no components
findings.detail: PLAN.md 7 requires named reward_components and PLAN.md 11.3 separates task score from training shaping. The vendored env computes a single scalar.
findings.impact: Reward decomposition cannot be reported until the task layer owns it.
findings.resolution: the adapter reports one component named `vendor_total` rather than inventing a decomposition it did not compute

deviations.from: PLAN.md M1: 'stub compiler artifact' in the walking skeleton
deviations.to: a real procgen compiler producer that reads the engine's own waypoint graph
deviations.reason: A hand-written stub would agree with nothing. Compiling from the graph the runtime navigates makes the skeleton prove the contracts connect, and seeds the M2 Paris producer.

deviations.to: a differing minor version is rejected while the package is 0.x
deviations.reason: PLAN.md M1 states there is no backward-compatibility promise before M12 and that early consumers pin exact schema revisions. Accepting 0.2 data into a 0.1 reader would contradict that. The 5.4 rule applies from 1.0.
